result.summary:
Ran `git diff origin/main...HEAD -- lib/letflow/tenant_provisioning.ex` directly. The diff is minimal: replay_migrations/2 gains a second `with`-clause step, `maybe_seed_entity_event_types(using_default_manifest?, schema_name)`, plus a new private function of the same name and an added `@spec` error variant `{:error, {:event_type_seed_failed, term()}}`. `schema_name` is the same value already bound from `%Registration{schema_name: schema_name} <- Repo.get_by(Registration, tenant_id: tenant_id)` at the top of the function and already used unmodified as `prefix: schema_name` in the pre-existing `Ecto.Migrator.run/4` call a few lines above -- no new untrusted input path, no new external parameter threaded in. Verdicts per invariant, against the actual diff:

INV-1 (tenant data isolation) -- APPLIES (S1 done, S2 migrations exist, diff touches a tenant-provisioning code path). Satisfied: (a) `Letflow.Entities.EventTypes.seed!/1` (`lib/letflow/entities/event_types.ex:117`, `def seed!(prefix) when is_binary(prefix)`) takes the schema name and registers event types through the existing `Letflow.EventStore.Registry.register_type/2` -- I read `seed!/1` and confirmed it receives `prefix` and does not bypass prefix-scoping; the added call site passes the already-prefix-derived `schema_name`, not a fresh/unscoped value. (b) no migration added in this diff -- N/A. (c) no `tenant_id` column write introduced by this diff -- N/A. No cross-tenant leak introduced: the new code path re-uses, and does not diverge from, the same `schema_name` already governing the tenant-scoped migration run in the same function.
INV-2 (server-side field auth) -- NOT-APPLICABLE. No API response type or field-serialisation code touched; S4 has not started.
INV-3 (untrusted runtime sandboxing) -- NOT-APPLICABLE. No Lua/WASM scripting code touched; S5 has not started.
INV-4 (secrets by reference only) -- APPLIES (live now). Ran `grep -rn "System.get_env" ...` and the hardcoded-secret heuristic scoped to the two touched files (`tenant_provisioning.ex`, `entities/event_types.ex`): zero hits in the added diff lines. The change introduces no secret material, no logging, no config/env resolution. PASS.
INV-5 (not-found/forbidden indistinguishability) -- NOT-APPLICABLE. No lookup-by-ID endpoint touched; S4 has not started.
INV-6 (new data-access paths prove their scoping) -- APPLIES (meta-invariant, always). Satisfied by this handoff itself: this is the SECURITY-REVIEWER gate proving INV-1's scoping explicitly rather than relying on ELIXIR-DEV's self-report, per the worked procedure above.
INV-7 (no SQL string interpolation) -- APPLIES (live now, Ecto in use). Ran `grep -rn "Repo.query" lib/ priv/repo/migrations/`. Multiple pre-existing hits in `tenant_provisioning.ex` (lines 307, 321, 1164, 1208, 1517, 1543, 1648, 1764, 1969, 2111, 2162, 2178, 2217) -- none of these lines are part of this diff (confirmed against the `git diff` hunk, which only touches lines ~368-403 and ~1085-1099, adding a `@spec` line, a `with`-clause line, and a new private function with no `Repo.query` call). The new private function `maybe_seed_entity_event_types/2` contains no SQL. PASS, nothing new to flag; pre-existing raw-SQL call sites are out of scope for this diff and were not introduced or modified by it.
INV-8 (no unhandled crashes on realistic failure paths) -- APPLIES (live now). Ran `grep -n "^\s*{:ok, .*} = "` scoped to the two touched files: only pre-existing hits at lines 324 and 671 of `tenant_provisioning.ex`, neither touched by this diff. The new code itself uses a `case ... do {:ok, _} -> :ok; {:error, reason} -> {:error, {...}} end` pattern inside `maybe_seed_entity_event_types/2` -- both branches of `seed!/1`'s return are handled explicitly, no bare match. The outer `with` chain's failure short-circuits into the function's existing `{:error, {:event_type_seed_failed, reason}}` tuple, which the caller can pattern-match on (new `@spec` variant added correctly). PASS.
INV-9 (outbound URL validation) -- NOT-APPLICABLE. No outbound HTTP request or tenant-controlled URL touched by this diff.

Overall: PASS. All applicable invariants (INV-1, INV-4, INV-6, INV-7, INV-8) satisfied against the actual diff; INV-2/INV-3/INV-5/INV-9 correctly NOT-APPLICABLE.
